note: Module-level master rules reconstructed from retained thread summary.

rules.rule: Profile before prescription: create a multidimensional athlete profile before generating training.
Treat body mass as functional mass relative to role; track it with composition and performance rather than assuming bigger is better.
Store absolute and relative strength because both can matter in rugby.
Store power as a distinct quality; power reflects force expressed at velocity.
Separate acceleration from maximal sprint speed and preserve split/test context.
Separate aerobic fitness, RSA, and RHIE instead of one generic endurance score.
Readiness is contextual and longitudinal: sleep, fatigue, soreness, stress, mental fatigue, mood, fueling and hydration inform but do not diagnose.
Treat social-media/cognitive-load information as optional context, never surveillance.
Individualize nutrition; use food-first practice, carb periodization where useful, and anti-doping/supplement-contamination safeguards. Do not hard-code a 45-minute anabolic window.
Use privacy-by-design, especially for minors and sensitive health information.
Distinguish global movement screens, local joint ROM, and dynamic control under speed/load/repetition.
Screening produces observations and hypotheses, not medical diagnosis.
Pain is a hard gate: stop the automated corrective pathway and refer appropriately.
Store protocol, side, result, units, pain, asymmetry, date, assessor, intervention and retest date.
Standardize camera position, height, distance, athlete orientation, landmarks, repetition/frame, surface and footwear.
Store vision-derived measures with confidence and image-quality flags.
Use 'possible contributor', 'suggests', 'may contribute' and 'consistent with'; do not assert unmeasured causal muscle diagnoses.
Repeated consistent findings increase hypothesis confidence; conflicting findings reduce it.
Treat 'overactive/underactive' labels as hypotheses only; video observes movement, not muscle activation.
Match intervention to the identified limitation; stretching alone does not solve strength/control deficits.
